raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Production fault tests for #45919 exposed an independent bug: a local GPU worker can exit while the HTTP server still advertises readiness. A multi-rank allocator OOM is worse: the failing rank resumes request dispatch while its peer remains in the previous forward, permanently desynchronizing the replica.

Both failures were reproduced on main (`4b273537dec`), independently of progress reporting.

## Changes

- Track launcher-owned worker process identities, including the WebUI HTTP child and locally launched disaggregated pools.
- Return readiness 503 after any owned worker exits, including zombie/PID-reuse cases. Keep HTTP liveness independent.
- Check owned processes once per second, terminate pending scheduler waits even without an RPC deadline, and reject new POST requests with 503. Completed job status/content remain readable.
- Treat allocator OOM during a multi-rank forward as fatal to the worker. Exit at the process boundary without potentially blocking CUDA/NCCL teardown; do not reuse the desynchronized replica.
- Preserve request-level OOM recovery for single-GPU replicas, including independent DP replicas.
- Document restart requirements and coverage limits. No extra GPU collective, per-step callback, CLI knob, or change to generated outputs.

## Validation

- Remote regression tests: the new client and multi-rank OOM cases fail before the fix (3 failed, 2 passed). Fixed related suite: **114 passed, 4 subtests passed**.
- Real 2x H200 tests, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 / CUDA 13.0 / Diffusers 0.37.0 / Transformers 5.19.0. Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers, 512x320, 17 frames, seed 42, 24 denoising steps after warmup.
- A separate GPU allocation leaves approximately 128 MiB free; an 832x480, 33-frame request triggers a real allocator OOM, not an injected exception.
- Ulysses=2: pressure on rank 0 and rank 1 tested separately. All three in-flight/queued jobs fail within **0.77 s / 0.66 s**, without an RPC deadline. TP=2 non-output-rank OOM: **0.94 s**. Readiness/new POSTs return 503; previous output remains downloadable and decodes to identical frames.
- Single GPU: three OOM/recovery cycles. DP=2: three cycles on **each** GPU. All nine recoveries preserve decoded frame hashes; normal readiness remains 200.
- SP outputs before failure match main's decoded frame hashes. No owned child processes remain after shutdown.
- Combined with #45919 on a detached validation head: real per-step progress and multi-rank OOM handling both pass. The independent fixes remain separate PRs.
- Earlier real worker-SIGKILL tests also covered the spawned HTTP bootstrap and a local encoder/denoiser/decoder pool with Mooncake transfers. Full Gradio UI was not tested.
- Pre-commit passes. No GT, tolerance, or performance baseline changes.

This is bounded failure handling, not transparent failover: restart the whole server and retry failed jobs. Arbitrary live-process hangs, remote-worker supervision, durable job recovery, and fatal CUDA-context errors remain separate concerns (#45065).

- Readiness now also tracks the disaggregation router thread and offline broker task. Router exit, broker bind failure, or fatal socket errors fail pending waits and reject new requests; existing outputs remain readable.

With the fix, readiness returns 503, liveness remains 200, and three pending jobs become failed within 1 second. SIGTERM exits normally. Before/after reference videos have identical decoded frames.

No new per-step collectives or GPU health probes. This reports unrecoverable local backend failures; it does not provide transparent failover or interrupt already-running GPU work. New-head CI is running.

Hi Mick, this looks great! It overlaps a bit with #45065 (fixes #38167). Once this lands, I'd be happy to rework #45065 to exit the worker on those errors and reuse your backend monitor, instead of adding a separate unhealthy flag.

@@ -452,14 +452,34 @@ SGLang Diffusion separates process liveness from inference readiness:
 | Endpoint | Success condition | Recommended use |
 | --- | --- | --- |
 | `GET /liveness` | The HTTP server is accepting requests. It remains `200` during server warmup. | Kubernetes liveness probe |
-| `GET /health` | The server is ready for normal inference traffic. It returns `503` while server-based synthetic warmup is running and `200` after it completes. | Startup and readiness probes |
+| `GET /health` | Server-based synthetic warmup has completed, tracked local workers are alive, and the local broker and any disaggregation routing loop are running. Returns `503` otherwise. | Startup and readiness probes |
 | `GET /health_generate` | Compatibility alias for `/health`. It does not currently issue a generation request in SGLang Diffusion. | Existing integrations only |
 
-`/health` gates only server-based warmup. With `--warmup-mode off` or
-`--warmup-mode request`, it returns `200` once the HTTP server starts; those modes
+With `--warmup-mode off` or `--warmup-mode request`, `/health` returns `200`
+once the HTTP server starts, provided its local backend is running; those modes
 do not promise that compilation or other first-request work has completed. If
 server-based warmup fails, the server terminates instead of reporting ready.
 
+For standard serving (including `--webui`) and locally launched disaggregated
+pools, losing any tracked worker makes `/health` return `503`; `/liveness`
+continues to report HTTP availability. The same applies when the local offline
+broker or disaggregation routing loop exits, even if its process is still alive.
+The broker replies to malformed jobs and inference errors without stopping;
+an unrecoverable socket receive or send error stops it and makes the server unready.
+A local monitor checks these components once per
+second, fails outstanding scheduler requests, and rejects new POST requests with
+`503`, even without an RPC timeout. Completed job status and content remain
+readable until the server stops. Remove the instance from routing and restart
+the whole server; workers and in-flight jobs are not automatically recovered.
+
+An allocator OOM during a multi-rank forward terminates the affected worker:
+other ranks may still be inside collectives, so continuing the next request is
+unsafe. Single-GPU replicas, including independent DP replicas, retain normal
+request-level OOM handling. The monitor does not detect arbitrary hangs, unusable
+CUDA contexts, or workers on other machines. A standalone disaggregation router
+does not own remote worker processes and cannot validate their health through this
+check; it only validates its own routing loop and broker.
+
 Do not use `/health` as a liveness probe: a long server warmup can legitimately
 keep it at `503` for several minutes.

Pushed the router/broker follow-up in b99060b46c15bab2fe2be7d8924bfb10deef646d after the previous head's NVIDIA CI completed successfully.

- Readiness now also tracks the disaggregation router thread and offline broker task. Router exit, broker bind failure, or fatal socket errors fail pending waits and reject new requests; existing outputs remain readable.
- Broker transport failures no longer enter an exception/retry busy loop. Individual malformed requests still receive errors without stopping the broker.
- Real H200 Wan2.1 tests reproduced the old failure: closing the broker socket drove the HTTP process to 99% CPU and made both health endpoints time out. With the fix, readiness returns 503, liveness remains 200, and three pending jobs become failed within 1 second. SIGTERM exits normally. Before/after reference videos have identical decoded frames.
- Local-pool and standalone-head router failures were also tested. Related remote suite: 94 passed, 6 subtests. The earlier router-focused suite and combined progress/readiness validation are unchanged.

No new per-step collectives or GPU health probes. This reports unrecoverable local backend failures; it does not provide transparent failover or interrupt already-running GPU work. New-head CI is running.

Hi Mick, this looks great! It overlaps a bit with #45065 (fixes #38167). Once this lands, I'd be happy to rework #45065 to exit the worker on those errors and reuse your backend monitor, instead of adding a separate unhealthy flag.
